title: Prove durable execution and reproducible packaging
frozen_note: This record is immutable. A later verification run does not edit it; it produces a new baseline_version. Nothing in this file is a claim that the system is calibrated, production-ready, or generally reliable.

clean_runner_starts_full_compose_stack.means: On a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner with volumes pruned first, `docker compose up -d --wait` brought every declared service to a running state from images pulled during that run.
clean_runner_starts_full_compose_stack.does_not_mean: Nothing about any other host, orchestrator, base image, or a run with warm caches. An unreachable registry fails this criterion; there is no static-validation fallback.

all_service_health_checks_pass.means: Every declared service reported `healthy` against its own Compose healthcheck, and scripts/health.py independently reached each service's documented health endpoint over the network.
all_service_health_checks_pass.does_not_mean: That any service behaves correctly beyond answering its health endpoint.

real_temporal_workflow_appears_and_compl.means: A workflow execution was created on the Temporal server at TEMPORAL_ADDRESS, was retrievable by its workflow ID, reached WorkflowExecutionStatus.COMPLETED, and its history was fetched back from the server.
real_temporal_workflow_appears_and_compl.does_not_mean: Anything about a production Temporal deployment. The server is `temporal server start-dev`.

coding_workflow_executes_under_temporal.means: CodingEvaluationWorkflow specifically — not only the purpose-built probe workflows — executed on the real server, crossed the validation conditional edge into the activity branch, produced at least one ACTIVITY_TASK_COMPLETED event, crossed the diagnosis conditional edge, and completed with a non-empty history inside a bounded timeout.
coding_workflow_executes_under_temporal.does_not_mean: Anything about the quality of a patch, or about graph paths not taken (the abstention branch is not exercised here).

worker_interruption_recovery.means: The first worker process was SIGKILLed after its checkpoint activity completed; the execution stayed RUNNING with no worker polling; a second worker process resumed it; it completed; and the append-only effect ledger held exactly one checkpoint row.
worker_interruption_recovery.does_not_mean: Recovery from loss of the Temporal server itself, or of its volume. Neither is exercised.

retry_behaviour_from_real_history.means: An activity induced to fail a fixed number of times was retried under the declared RetryPolicy. The attempt count read from ActivityTaskStarted.attempt in server-fetched history matched the expected count and the durable ledger, and exactly one consequential effect was committed.
retry_behaviour_from_real_history.does_not_mean: That history contains one event per failed attempt — Temporal does not write those. The attempt count comes from the attempt field, cross-checked against our own ledger.

timeout_behaviour.means: An activity that exceeded its start_to_close_timeout produced an ActivityTaskTimedOut event in real history, and the harness surfaced it as an infrastructure failure.
timeout_behaviour.does_not_mean: That every timeout class is covered. Only start-to-close on an activity is exercised.

replay_determinism_verification.means: temporalio.worker.Replayer — the SDK's supported facility, not a hand-written history parser — replayed a real recorded history against the workflow definition that produced it without error, and raised a nondeterminism error for a deliberately incompatible variant of that workflow.
replay_determinism_verification.does_not_mean: Determinism of any workflow other than the one replayed, or of that workflow under inputs it has not seen.

phoenix_contains_required_spans.means: A query to the running Phoenix instance returned at least one trace for the project, and the observed span-name set contained every required span name.
phoenix_contains_required_spans.does_not_mean: That parent/child span nesting is correct. Nesting across the workflow/activity process boundary is not asserted anywhere.

ducttape_remains_rejected.means: Under execution_mode=temporal the duct-tape candidate recorded outcome `rejected`, its failing gate set included not_symptom_suppression, and its observed effect invocation count was 2 — the same expectation Task 1 asserted, unrelaxed.
ducttape_remains_rejected.does_not_mean: That the system detects symptom suppression in general. One candidate, one fixture, one bug class.

known_good_remains_accepted_for_review.means: Under execution_mode=temporal the known-good candidate recorded outcome `accepted_for_review` with no failing gate and an effect invocation count of 1, and the report recorded merged_or_deployed=false.
known_good_remains_accepted_for_review.does_not_mean: `accepted_for_review` is the only positive outcome in this system and it means a human should look. It is never `approved`, `correct`, `safe`, or `production_ready`, and nothing was merged, pushed, or deployed.

infrastructure_failures_classified_separ.means: A real infrastructure fault (the activity timeout) was classified as infrastructure_failure by both the workflow and the reliability layer, and was not reported as a defective patch.
infrastructure_failures_classified_separ.does_not_mean: That every infrastructure fault class is classified correctly. One induced fault is exercised.

state_persists_across_restart.means: After `docker compose stop` followed by `up` on the existing volumes, previously created workflow executions were still describable with unchanged history event counts, and Phoenix still returned traces for the project.
state_persists_across_restart.does_not_mean: Survival of volume deletion, host loss, or an upgrade of either service.

dependencies_and_images_pinned.means: Every declared Python dependency is exactly pinned with ==, every Compose image carries an @sha256: digest, installed versions matched what is declared, and zero problems were recorded.
dependencies_and_images_pinned.does_not_mean: That the pinned versions are free of vulnerabilities, or that a digest still resolves at a registry today.

state_initialisation.means: The audit store and the privileged identity store exist as separate database files, and the Temporal namespace is registered.
state_initialisation.does_not_mean: That the separation is enforced by the operating system. It is structural; code with filesystem access can still open either file.

limitations.limitation: One hosted run, not a standing guarantee
limitations.detail: The acceptance contract above records a single execution on a single day. The completion manifest is generated per run from evidence files; a later run can report fewer criteria. A green history is not a property of the system.

All durability evidence comes from `temporal server start-dev` with SQLite persistence, running as root in its container so it can create that database in a fresh named volume. Nothing here transfers to a production Temporal deployment.
Recovery is demonstrated for an abrupt SIGKILL of the worker process while the server stayed up.
Losing the Temporal server, or its persistence volume, is not exercised at all. The restart test stops and starts services against volumes that remain intact.

Phoenix evidence asserts that the required span names are present, not that spans are correctly nested. Activity-side nodes run in a different process, and correct parent/child linkage there depends on Temporal's OpenTelemetry interceptor, which is installed but unverified.
Patch bodies come from the fixture's own candidate library, not from a model; the models are deterministic mocks behind LiteLLM. No model wrote a patch, and no live provider was contacted.

limitations.limitation: No calibration and no benchmark generalization
limitations.detail: One fixture, one planted bug (a check-then-write race under at-least-once delivery), two candidates. There is no calibration of any judgment, no benchmark, and no basis for extrapolating to other defects.

explicitly_not_claimed: any bug class beyond the single duplicate-processing fixture
correctness or safety of any patch that reached accepted_for_review
